subject: biology
title: Monohybrid inheritance
key_idea: A gene has different forms called alleles. The genotype is the alleles an organism carries; the phenotype is how they show, together with the environment. Alleles can be dominant, recessive or codominant, and a genetic diagram predicts the offspring of a cross.

blocks.text: Every genetics question uses the same vocabulary. This section defines it.

items.meaning: A length of DNA at a particular place on a chromosome that codes for a polypeptide.
The position of a gene on a chromosome.
One of the different forms of a gene. There may be many alleles of one gene.
The genetic constitution of an organism: the alleles it carries.
The expression of the genotype and its interaction with the environment.
Having two identical alleles at a locus in a diploid organism.
Having two different alleles at a locus in a diploid organism.

blocks.text: A diploid organism has two copies of each chromosome, so it has two alleles at each locus. One comes from each parent.

items: Genotype is the alleles; phenotype is how they are expressed.
Homozygous means two identical alleles; heterozygous means two different alleles.
A gene can have more than two alleles in a population, but one individual carries only two.

blocks.text: Alleles differ in how they show in a heterozygote. There are three patterns.

items: A **dominant** allele is expressed in the phenotype when only one copy is present.
A **recessive** allele is expressed only when two copies are present, so there is no dominant allele to mask it.
**Codominant** alleles are both expressed in the phenotype of a heterozygote. Neither masks the other.

blocks.text: Multiple alleles: the ABO blood groups
The ABO gene has three alleles: Iᴬ, Iᴮ and i. Iᴬ and Iᴮ are codominant. Both are dominant to i.

items: Dominant: expressed with one copy. Recessive: needs two copies.
Codominant alleles are both expressed in a heterozygote.
ABO shows multiple alleles and codominance together.

blocks.text: A monohybrid cross follows one gene. A fully labelled genetic diagram shows the parents, their gametes, the offspring genotypes and the offspring phenotypes.

items.text: Choose a letter for each allele. Write the genotype of each parent.
Each gamete carries one allele, because meiosis separates the pair. Write the gametes in circles.
Join each gamete from one parent to each gamete from the other, for example in a Punnett square.
Say what each genotype looks like. Give the ratio, or the probability, of each phenotype.

blocks.text: Use the cross below to see the ratios for yourself.

diagram.alt: A Punnett square tool. Choose a genotype for each parent, with R for round seeds and r for wrinkled seeds, and see the offspring genotypes and phenotypes.

rows: All carry at least one R

blocks.text: These ratios are probabilities. Real offspring numbers are rarely exactly in the ratio, because fertilisation is random.

items: Parents, gametes, offspring genotypes, offspring phenotypes: label every stage.
Heterozygous × heterozygous gives 3 : 1 for a dominant and recessive pair.
Ratios are probabilities, not guarantees.

blocks.text: An organism with the dominant phenotype could be homozygous or heterozygous. A **test cross** finds out which.

items: Cross the organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive organism.
If any offspring show the recessive phenotype, the unknown parent was heterozygous. The expected ratio is 1 : 1.
If all the offspring show the dominant phenotype, the unknown parent was probably homozygous dominant.
A large number of offspring is needed to be confident the parent was homozygous.
Test cross: unknown dominant phenotype × homozygous recessive.
Any recessive offspring means the parent was heterozygous.
Only dominant offspring suggests homozygous, more strongly with more offspring.

checks.a: Genotype is the alleles an organism carries (its genetic constitution). Phenotype is the expression of the genotype and its interaction with the environment.

checks.q: A woman with blood group A (genotype Iᴬi) and a man with blood group B (genotype Iᴮi) have a child. State the possible blood groups of the child and the probability of blood group O.
checks.a: Gametes: Iᴬ or i from the mother, Iᴮ or i from the father. Offspring: IᴬIᴮ (AB), Iᴬi (A), Iᴮi (B), ii (O), each equally likely. Possible groups A, B, AB and O. Probability of O = 1 in 4 (25%).

checks.q: A plant with the dominant phenotype is crossed with a homozygous recessive plant. The offspring are 52 with the dominant phenotype and 48 with the recessive phenotype. State the genotype of the first plant and explain your answer.
checks.a: It is heterozygous. The offspring are in a ratio of about 1 : 1. Recessive offspring must have received a recessive allele from each parent, so the first plant carried one recessive allele. If it were homozygous dominant, all the offspring would show the dominant phenotype.

blocks.text: With **incomplete dominance** neither allele is fully dominant. The heterozygote has a phenotype between the two homozygotes.

items: Example: a red-flowered plant crossed with a white-flowered plant gives all pink offspring.
Crossing two pink plants gives 1 red : 2 pink : 1 white.
This differs from codominance, where both alleles are seen separately in the heterozygote.

blocks.text: A pedigree shows who in a family has a trait. Squares are males, circles are females and shaded symbols are affected.

items: Two unaffected parents with an affected child: the trait is recessive, and both parents are heterozygous carriers.
Two affected parents with an unaffected child: the trait is dominant, and both parents are heterozygous.
An affected child needs the affected allele from a parent, so check each parent in turn.
Give the genotype of each person where it can be worked out, and say which individuals could be either.

items.meaning: The first filial generation: the offspring of the parental cross.
The second filial generation: the offspring when F1 individuals are crossed with each other.
Genes on the same chromosome that tend to be inherited together.
A cross between an organism of unknown genotype and a homozygous recessive organism.

items: Pure-breeding parents (RR × rr) give an F1 that is all Rr.
Crossing F1 with F1 gives an F2 of 3 dominant : 1 recessive.
Genetic diagrams must also cope with codominance, multiple alleles and sex linkage, using the same four stages.
Dihybrid crosses and sex linkage are covered in the next note.
